metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Romania strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking... maybe we could get some lilies for Emily? They seem nice for a celebration, right? 

Also, I wanted to ask you something. Do you think making our parents proud should be a main goal in life? I... I don't really feel that way.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Lilies sound good, but I think something more personal might be better. Maybe a nice book or something related to her major? 

As for making our parents proud, well... for me, it’s really important. It’s like a way to honor everything they’ve done for us. I just can’t imagine not having that as a main goal.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
A book could work, I guess... but lilies are pretty meaningful too. I just think flowers bring a certain *joy* to celebrations, you know? 

But about the whole making parents proud thing... I mean, can’t we also focus on what *we* want? It seems too much pressure to make that the main goal.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I get what you mean about flowers bringing joy, but you know, at the end of the day it's all the same. A book could also bring happiness, just in a different way. 

As for making parents proud, I don’t really see meaningful differences here. I think people figure it out in their own ways. I just feel like everyone has their own path, and that's cool. Doesn't matter to me how we approach it. So, what do you think about picking a book for Emily instead?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
Yeah, I see how a book could bring happiness... but lilies just feel more celebratory to me. 

And about the whole parents proud thing... I guess I just think it shouldn't be all about that. It's a lot to carry. Maybe we should just focus on what makes *us* happy instead of what others expect. So... can we stick with the lilies?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:

While I appreciate the importance of personal happiness, I believe I can find joy in making my parents proud. It's like a balance—I can pursue what I love while still valuing my family's support. So, back to Emily's gift, do you think we can agree on a nice book then?
